newsitem.title: USA: Dakota, Minnesota railroad in $1.2 billion expansion.
newsitem.headline: Dakota, Minnesota railroad in $1.2 billion expansion.

text.p: Dakota, Minnesota & Eastern Railroad Corp. said Monday it plans a $1.2 billion track expansion into a prime coal mining region of northeastern Wyoming.
As part of the project, the railroad will build 250 miles of track into the Powder River Basin of Wyoming, a prime source of coal that helps power plants meet pollution standards for emissions.
In addition, the railroad said it plans to rebuild about 650 miles of existing track. The project should be completed within five years, it said.

"There is rapidly growing demand for the Powder River Basin's inexpensive, environmentally friendly, low-sulphur coal," Kevin Schieffer, president, said in a statement. "Implementation of Phase II of the Clean Air Act Amendments affects all coal-fired power plants, mandating additional reductions in sulphur emissions."
